title: Integrative Bioinformatics Analysis Reveals Key Regulatory Genes and Therapeutic Targets in Ulcerative Colitis Pathogenesis.
authors: Rahman, Sheikh Atikur; Khatun, Mst Tania; Singh, Mahendra; Biswas, Viplov Kumar; Hoque, Forkanul; Zaman, Nurun Nesa; Parvin, Anzana; Uddin, Mohammad Khaja Mafij; Sheikh, Md Mominul Islam; Begum, Most Morium; Arya, Rakesh; Faruquee, Hossain Md
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过生物信息学分析溃疡性结肠炎差异表达基因并构建PPI网络，虽提及转录因子和分子对接，但核心是疾病标志物筛选而非蛋白质-DNA互作机制建模，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ulcerative colitis (UC), a chronic and relapsing form of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), arises from a multifactorial interplay of genetic predisposition, immune dysregulation, and environmental triggers. Despite advances in understanding UC pathogenesis, the identification of reliable biomarkers and key regulatory genes remains essential for unraveling disease mechanisms. Such insights are crucial for improving diagnostic precision and developing personalized therapeutic strategies. METHODS: In this study, gene expression profiles from publicly available microarray and RNA-sequencing datasets were systematically analyzed using advanced bioinformatics tools. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified through statistical comparisons, and functional enrichment analyses were performed to explore their biological relevance. A total of 141 overlapping DEGs were extracted from three GEO datasets, and 20 key DEGs were further prioritized via protein-protein interaction (PPI) network construction. Hub genes, relevant signaling pathways, associated transcription factors (TFs), and microRNAs (miRNAs) linked to disease progression were identified. Potential therapeutic compounds were also predicted through computational drug-gene interaction analysis. RESULTS: The analysis revealed a panel of novel biomarkers-TLR2, IFNG, CD163, CXCL9, CCL4, PRF1, TLR8, ARG1, LILRB2, FPR2, and PPARG-that function as key hub genes implicated in ulcerative colitis (UC) pathogenesis. These genes were associated with critical biological processes including signal transduction, inflammatory and immune responses, proteolysis, lipid transport, and cholesterol/triglyceride homeostasis. Furthermore, transcription factors (FOXC1, GABPA, GATA2, SUPT5H) and microRNAs (hsa-miR-34a-5p, hsa-miR-335-5p, hsa-miR-24-3p, hsa-miR-23a-5p, hsa-miR-26a-5p) revealed key regulatory networks influencing post-transcriptional gene regulation. Molecular docking analysis predicted Apremilast and Golotimod as promising therapeutic candidates for UC intervention. CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion, this study enhances our understanding of ulcerative colitis pathogenesis by identifying key biomarkers and therapeutic targets, paving the way for future advancements in personalized diagnosis and treatment strategies.
abstract_zh: 背景：溃疡性结肠炎（UC）是一种慢性、复发性炎症性肠病（IBD），其发病源于遗传易感性、免疫失调和环境触发因素的多因素相互作用。尽管在理解UC发病机制方面取得了进展，但识别可靠的生物标志物和关键调控基因对于阐明疾病机制仍至关重要。这些见解对于提高诊断精确性和制定个性化治疗策略至关重要。方法：在本研究中，利用先进的生物信息学工具系统分析了公开可用的微阵列和RNA测序数据集中的基因表达谱。通过统计比较鉴定了差异表达基因（DEGs），并进行功能富集分析以探索其生物学相关性。从三个GEO数据集中提取了141个重叠的DEGs，并通过蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络构建进一步优先筛选出20个关键DEGs。鉴定了与疾病进展相关的枢纽基因、相关信号通路、相关转录因子（TFs）和微小RNA（miRNAs）。还通过计算药物-基因相互作用分析预测了潜在的治疗化合物。结果：分析揭示了一组新型生物标志物——TLR2、IFNG、CD163、CXCL9、CCL4、PRF1、TLR8、ARG1、LILRB2、FPR2和PPARG——它们作为与溃疡性结肠炎（UC）发病机制相关的关键枢纽基因发挥作用。这些基因与关键生物过程相关，包括信号转导、炎症和免疫反应、蛋白水解、脂质运输以及胆固醇/甘油三酯稳态。此外，转录因子（FOXC1、GABPA、GATA2、SUPT5H）和微小RNA（hsa-miR-34a-5p、hsa-miR-335-5p、hsa-miR-24-3p、hsa-miR-23a-5p、hsa-miR-26a-5p）揭示了影响转录后基因调控的关键调控网络。分子对接分析预测阿普斯特（Apremilast）和戈洛替莫德（Golotimod）是UC干预的有前景的治疗候选药物。结论：总之，本研究通过识别关键生物标志物和治疗靶点，增进了我们对溃疡性结肠炎发病机制的理解，为未来个性化诊断和治疗策略的进步铺平了道路。
